$comment: Written reasons for the capabilities catalogue (docs/DSL_CAPABILITIES.html), batch 6 of N, 2026-11-23 (REG-357, owner: do only 20% of the remaining cases, of mixed complexity). One reason per keyword: what need it serves and why a lower rung of the extension ladder (expression, function, flow step, hand-written code) or an existing keyword cannot do it. The reasons state the need, not the evidence counts: the catalogue's own columns show samples, tests and examples and change as the corpus grows, so a count written here would go stale. The batch is every 5th keyword still without a reason, taken within each kind of value (boolean, text, number, choice, list, object, reference) so simple and complex ones are mixed. Key = slot id exactly as the catalogue shows it; the generator refuses a reason for a keyword the schema does not have.

reasons.guidePageRegion.defaultCollapsed: A guide page with a long optional section reads better when that section starts folded and the main text stays in view; the flag sets the starting state and the reader can still open the region.
reasons.property.securityRelevant: A signing secret or a payment key must never be copied into a rule that decides who may read or write; marking the property makes the validator refuse any such rule and flags it for an elevated role in the admin screen, a guarantee over all rules that no single expression can give.
reasons.field.required: A customer without a name is useless, so the value must be supplied on create and never cleared; one flag makes the form, the API and the database agree, where an invariant would only catch the gap afterwards. On an object field a list of names says which inner properties are required.
reasons.panelAction.binding: A button on a generated screen must run something; the binding says whether it runs a stored query, a mutation or a flow, so the screen stays declarative and the button needs no hand-written handler.
reasons.schemaObject.type: A command's arguments or an event's payload must say what each value is, so a wrong one is refused before any code runs; the type names the kind of value, a scalar, an object, an array or a reference, and nothing else carries it.
reasons.concept.indexes: A list of orders filtered by customer and date slows down as rows grow; the platform already indexes ids and unique fields, and this lists the extra ones, which only the author who knows the queries can choose. No expression or flow can shape the database.
reasons.flow.steps: A business process such as approving an order is an ordered series of actions; the step list is that order, so the engine can run, pause, retry and resume it from the recorded point instead of a hand-written method that loses its place on restart.
reasons.humanTask.outcomes: A person approving a request needs buttons such as approve or reject; the list gives each button its stored value and its label, and the chosen one is recorded and published so the flow can branch on it.
reasons.pack:packs: A pack that builds on other packs must say which ones and at what minimum version, so installing it brings in what it needs and refuses a version that is too old; a hand-installed dependency would be forgotten and fail late.
reasons.panelLayout.widgets: A dashboard needs tiles, charts and tables side by side, computed over the panel's own data; the widget list declares them, so a console is composed rather than coded as a page, and a hand-made page stays available for what widgets cannot show.
reasons.root:domainTypes: Fifty fields that all hold a tax code should not each repeat its length and pattern; a domain type names that field type once and fields refer to it, so the rule changes in one place.
reasons.root:seeds: A new app needs its first rows, such as default categories, present at first start; seeds declare them in the model and the platform applies them once through the same governed save path as any write, so no setup script is needed.
reasons.flowStep.maxLoopIterations: A step that repeats over a list can run away when the list is huge or wrongly built; the cap stops it at a number the author chooses, so one bad input cannot hold the process forever.
reasons.schemaObject.min: A quantity must not be negative and a percentage must stay in range; the smallest allowed number is checked at the boundary, before the value reaches any rule or storage, and every caller is told the same thing.
reasons.flowStep.data: An event announcing that an order shipped must carry some values, some literal and some read from the flow state; an object built in place states them without an earlier step whose only job is to assemble the payload.
reasons.pack:forkedFrom: A pack copied from another and improved should say whose work it started from and at which version, so the original author is credited and a user can trace back to the source; the registry reads it instead of guessing from free text.
reasons.root:provides: A pack may require roles, capabilities or network access, and the app that installs it must say which of those it satisfies; an unbound requirement refuses the composition and names the pack and the missing key, so nothing runs silently without what it needs.
reasons.concept.ui: How a concept looks as a whole, its labels, form layout, default grouping and whether writes work offline, is presentation and not data; one block keeps those hints apart from the fields so the data model stays clean.
reasons.flowStep.task: Some waits are for a person: a manager must approve before the flow goes on. A task on an awaitEvent step lists it in the assignee's inbox with a form, a due date and outcomes, and completing it resumes the flow; without it the author would build an inbox by hand.
reasons.queryParameter.schema: A query parameter that is itself structured, such as a date range or a list of ids, needs the same typed description as any other input; pointing at a schema object gives it, where a plain type could describe only one value.
reasons.aggregateCollectionLookupField.joinField: An order line should show the product's current name, which lives in another query's rows; naming a field present on both sides joins them in memory when the aggregate loads, with no lookup per row.
reasons.autoPanel.route: Every generated screen must live at an address people can bookmark and share; the route is its address segment, chosen by the author so the address stays stable when the screen is renamed.
reasons.capabilityOperationError.name: A caller of an outside operation must tell a refused card from a timeout; each declared error has a name callers can match, so a flow can branch on a known code instead of reading message text.
reasons.conversion.concept: When a field is renamed, split or merged, the rows already stored must be rewritten once at start-up to the new shape; the conversion names the concept whose rows are rewritten, so the migration runs in the same ordered path as the change itself, without hand-written SQL.
reasons.documentColumn.label: A printed invoice should say Unit price, not the field's name; the label is the column heading on the page and defaults to the field name, so the document reads like a document without renaming the field.
reasons.field.description: A person filling in a form and an AI writing a model both need one sentence on what a field holds; the description is shown as help in the generated screen and read by AI authors, so the sentence is written once.
reasons.flowSchedule.cron: A nightly clean-up or a Monday report must start at set times without anyone pressing a button; the cron expression says when, in the notation operators already know, and the platform's scheduler starts the flow.
reasons.flowStep.operation: A flow that calls an outside capability, such as charging a card, must say which of its operations; the name picks one operation of the named capability, so the call is checked against what the capability declares.
reasons.guidePageTheme.logoUrl: A guide page shown to customers should carry the company's logo; the image address goes in the theme, so the page's look is configuration and not a copy of the page template.
reasons.inboundDoor.idempotencyKey: A payment provider that retries a delivery must not create the order twice; the key says where in the body or the headers the delivery's unique id sits, so a repeat is acknowledged and ignored instead of processed again.
reasons.pack:description: Someone browsing a pack catalogue must tell in one sentence what a pack provides before installing it; the description is that sentence, read by the catalogue and by AI authors choosing packs.
reasons.panelAction.name: Buttons on a screen must be told apart in the model, the API and any rule that refers to them; the name is that handle, unique within the panel so a reference is never ambiguous.
reasons.panelFieldBinding.visibleWhen: A field such as the rejection reason should appear only while the status is Rejected; an expression evaluated as the person edits shows or hides it, so the form follows the data without a hand-written script.
reasons.presentationMetadata.imageField: A reference picker that shows a product should show its photo, not only its name; naming the target's image field uses it as the thumbnail of the selected value.
reasons.query.where: A list of open orders for the current user must filter rows by a condition that uses the query's parameters; the where expression states it, and the concept's row-level access still applies on top, so a filter can never widen what a person may see.
reasons.referenceDefinition.previewCardTemplate: When someone picks a customer in a form, a small card with name, phone and balance helps confirm the choice; the template says what the card shows, so a reference field looks right without a custom widget.
reasons.transactionDerivedField.procedure: A total that needs a server rule, such as tax by region, cannot be computed in the browser; on the server tier, naming the flow to run over the draft keeps that rule in one place, on the server.
